card.name: Gato
card.era: Emerged c. 1820s-1830s; peak gaucho popularity mid-19th century
card.tagline: Playful, picaresque gaucho couple dance with humorous verses.
card.profile: The gato ('cat') is a lively, picaresque couples folk dance and music style, hugely popular across rural Argentina and a favorite of gaucho culture. Its rhythm resembles the chacarera but its structure differs; couples perform stomping, spinning, finger-snapping and 'relaciones' (humorous recited couplets when the music stops). It is played on guitar with sung verses; variants include the gato cuyano, patriótico, valseado, and polqueado (English Wikipedia).
card.insight: The gato was among the most popular dances of independence-era Argentina and strongly influenced the chacarera; Britannica lists it among the core gaucho couple dances based on the fandango (Encyclopædia Britannica).
card.image_significance: The gauchos' picaresque couple dance. A representative image shows colorful regional costume and lively partner or troupe footwork — pampas, Argentina.
